note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · RAISED WOOLLY HEADS
tiles.details: A perennial of dry limestone or gravel, often 10–30 cm tall. Slender, mostly leafless stalks carry compact oval or club-shaped heads ABOVE a basal fan of narrow folded leaves. The actual target-species Joey habit photographs (panels 0–1) and Tom Chester in-ground growth photograph (panel 3) teach the raised-head silhouette. Panel 3 does not expose connected roots, and none of these photographs measures individual glumes or lemmas.
tiles.short: Short dense pale heads stand above a low leafy tuft
tiles.status: ACTUAL TARGET PHOTOS — GROSS CLUE; ROOT CONNECTION UNVERIFIED

tiles.heading: 02 · FOLDED WHITE-EDGED BLADES
tiles.details: Inspect basal blades, often 1–2 mm wide in Kew's description, folded with pale firm/cartilaginous margins and pointed tips. Tom Chester's real close foliage photograph (panel 4) shows those white-edged blades, while panel 1 connects the blades to the flowering tuft. Neither panel supplies a verified millimeter width or keel cross-section; obtain a same-plant 10× leaf-edge/keel image with ruler.
tiles.short: Narrow folded leaves with stiff pale margins
tiles.status: ACTUAL WHITE-EDGED LEAF PHOTO — MEASUREMENT STILL NEEDED

tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE HAIR LIGULE
tiles.details: Panel 8 is a real target-species OUTER blade–sheath junction with conspicuous white collar hairs. It does NOT expose the true inner ligule. Open a fresh collar and distinguish the attached ligule hair fringe from longer surrounding collar hairs. Published ligule-fringe lengths differ: about 0.35 mm in the UT Williamson County account, ~0.5 mm in Kew GrassBase, and 2–3.5 mm in another regional treatment. Photograph the free inner edge with a 1-mm ruler; do not put a ligule arrow on the exterior hair tuft.
tiles.short: Hair fringe at the INNER blade–sheath junction, not a broad membrane
tiles.status: ACTUAL EXTERIOR COLLAR PHOTO — TRUE INNER LIGULE STILL MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · COUNT FLORETS INSIDE ONE SPIKELET
tiles.details: One woolly terminal head holds SEVERAL spikelets, each containing MULTIPLE florets. Panels 2 and 5 show genuine overlapping hairy reproductive units; panel 6 shows a greener attached stage and panel 7 a silvery mature stage. These photos improve recognition but do not prove a count of florets inside ONE isolated spikelet. Local UT treatment reports about 6–11 mm mature spikelets and 4–12 florets; broader treatments describe up to about 16 mm and more florets. Isolate and measure one mature spikelet at 10–20× before labeling a count.
tiles.short: Several woolly spikelets per head; multiple florets per spikelet
tiles.status: ACTUAL REPRODUCTIVE PHOTOS — CALIBRATED FLORET COUNT MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · GLUMES VS HAIRY LEMMA
tiles.details: Separate TWO relatively smooth, one-veined glumes from a single fertile floret. Kew describes glumes roughly 4.5–6 mm and fertile lemmas roughly 4.5–6 mm; the three-veined hairy lemma has a shallow apical notch and ONE short awn, commonly ~0.5–2.5 mm in the local treatment. Panels 2, 5 and 7 show real woolly floral material but NOT a calibrated, separated glume/lemma/awn series. Do not label generic head hairs as glume hairs or assert vein counts from overlapping bracts.
tiles.short: Two relatively smooth 1-veined glumes; hairy 3-veined fertile lemmas
tiles.status: ACTUAL HAIRY FLORAL PHOTOS — DISSECTION AND MEASUREMENTS MISSING

tiles.heading: 06 · CHECK THE LOOK-ALIKES
tiles.details: Panel 3 shows the target species' raised compact woolly head. Panel 9 is OTHER SPECIES Munroa pulchella (fluffgrass), whose woolly units sit DOWN among sharply pointed ground-level leaves. Panel 10 is OTHER SPECIES Tridens texanus, with a loose branched panicle and more separated hanging spikelets. Erioneuron avenaceum is a further unpictured look-alike: its lemma notch is generally deeper (~1–2.5 mm versus ~0–0.5 mm in the local E. pilosum account) and the upper glume can reach the lowest floret. Aristida threeawns have three awn limbs from one lemma. Use a mature dissection before deciding a close woollygrass species; uncertain sterile plants stay provisional.
tiles.short: Raised woolly club ≠ ground-level fluffgrass; one awn ≠ threeawn
tiles.status: ACTUAL OTHER-SPECIES PANELS 9–10 — E. AVENACEUM MICRO COMPARISON STILL MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: HAIRY WOOLLYGRASS — SHORT, UPRIGHT WHITE HEADS ABOVE A LOW TUFT. Look for a small warm-season perennial clump, often 10–30 cm tall on shallow limestone or gravel, with tight narrow folded leaves bearing pale/white hardened margins. Thin, mostly leafless flower stalks rise above the basal blades, ending in small dense pale-to-purplish, club-shaped heads of SEVERAL closely packed, woolly spikelets. A mature spikelet typically has 4–12 florets in the UT Williamson County material; each fertile lemma has THREE hairy veins, fine long hairs below, a tiny apical notch and ONE short awn. The two relatively smooth glumes are SHORTER than the lowermost floret. The true leaf collar LIGULE IS A FRINGE OF HAIRS (very short in the UT local treatment), NOT a large membrane. Confirm the glumes/lemma/awn under 10–20×, not from an overview photo.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: FIELD HABIT FIRST: use Tom Chester's credited whole in-ground Arizona photo to follow the leafy cluster at ground level up the flowering culm to a compact woolly head. The root attachment is not exposed.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Panel 8 is a real target-species OUTER blade–sheath junction with conspicuous white collar hairs. It does NOT expose the true inner ligule. Open a fresh collar and distinguish the attached ligule hair fringe from longer surrounding collar hairs. Published ligule-fringe lengths differ: about 0.35 mm in the UT Williamson County account, ~0.5 mm in Kew GrassBase, and 2–3.5 mm in another regional treatment. Photograph the free inner edge with a 1-mm ruler; do not put a ligule arrow on the exterior hair tuft.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: One woolly terminal head holds SEVERAL spikelets, each containing MULTIPLE florets. Panels 2 and 5 show genuine overlapping hairy reproductive units; panel 6 shows a greener attached stage and panel 7 a silvery mature stage. These photos improve recognition but do not prove a count of florets inside ONE isolated spikelet. Local UT treatment reports about 6–11 mm mature spikelets and 4–12 florets; broader treatments describe up to about 16 mm and more florets. Isolate and measure one mature spikelet at 10–20× before labeling a count.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: FLUFFGRASS / Munroa pulchella (syn. Dasyochloa pulchella): hugs the ground as a radiating, sometimes stoloniferous, very low spiky mat; dense woolly spikelet packets nest DOWN among pungent pointed leaves, not atop long mostly leafless erect stalks. TEXAS TRIDENS / Tridens texanus: a more open/flexuous branched panicle with spaced, hanging multiple-flowered spikelets and often bare lower portions of its panicle branches; it is NOT the short dense club of Erioneuron. LARGE-FLOWERED WOOLLYGRASS / Erioneuron avenaceum: can also carry stalked compact woolly heads; in a mature dissection the lemma notch is DEEPER (about 1–2.5 mm) and its upper glume often reaches or passes the lowest floret, compared with E. pilosum's shallow ~0–0.5 mm notch and both glumes shorter than the lowest floret. GENERAL THREEAWNS / Aristida spp.: three long awn limbs arise from one lemma, unlike hairy woollygrass's one short awn. Color, white hairs, dry gravel habitat and tuft height alone cannot decide identity.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: GREEN REPRODUCTIVE STAGE · real attached immature spikelets and narrow blades
panels.caption: Turner Brockman's photograph of Erioneuron pilosum depicts a real young upright flowering head with narrow overlapping green spikelet units and pale margins, above nearby true narrow leaves. Follow the flowerhead axis and later compare to the fully silvery mature floret photograph; it is not a dissected single lemma or a ruler-calibrated glume-vein image.
panels.creator: Turner Brockman
panels.modifications: RGB re-encoded clean JPEG no EXIF/GPS; arrows separate web layer
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

panels.label: 5 · TEXAS TRIDENS LOOK-ALIKE — loose hanging flower branches
panels.caption: TEXAS TRIDENS, NOT hairy woollygrass. The flowering head has long exposed branching segments and separate hanging multi-flowered spikelet clusters. Contrast that OPEN, arching construction with Erioneuron's compact tuft of several short pale woolly spikelets at the end of a nearly bare culm.
panels.creator: Gaiacoyote
panels.annotation_note: Hays Botany displays overlaid numbered anatomy pointers; the source JPEG itself is unchanged.

memory_rule: SHORT LOW TUFT + WHITE-MARGINED FOLDED LEAVES + SEPARATE LONG MOSTLY BARE STALKS WITH TIGHT WOOLLY HEADS = Erioneuron candidate. Confirm the SHORTER glumes, HAIRY 3-NERVED lemmas with ONE SHORT AWN and HAIR-FRINGED ligule.
safety_note: CURRENT 2026-10-28 GALLERY INVENTORY: 10 archived exact-species image records, but one Calvin King owner photo is PRIVATE-ONLY and is excluded from public teaching panels. Nine exact-species public-eligible teaching panels (indices 0–8) plus two explicitly different-species comparisons (Munroa at 9, Tridens texanus at 10) = 11 panels. Existing visible-only markers are preserved; source rights include Joey CC BY-NC, Tom Chester's exact-page credited permission (NOT CC), Turner Brockman CC BY-SA, Beth CC BY-NC, and Michelle W CC BY. The exterior collar (8) does not demonstrate the inner ligule. Hairy head photographs (2,5,7) do not demonstrate measured glumes, lemma veins, notch, awn insertion, or an independently counted single spikelet. A rooted same-plant series, inner hair-fringe ligule with 1-mm ruler, and separated mature spikelet/lemma with scale remain necessary. No new photos or arrow coordinates were added and no Pages deployment was verified.
field_rule: Compact white/purplish woolly heads on slender largely bare flowering culms ABOVE a low tuft of folded white-edged leaves; verify smooth short glumes versus a THREE-NERVED hairy one-awned lemma.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
